name: Resonator
description: Strings stretched down a corridor and sighted along, arranged in a barrel around the camera so they converge on a vanishing point. Each stands in its own mode — one half-wave for the fundamental, more for every partial above it — with the nodes beaded on the string where it never moves. Tuned across the spectrum and driven by the band followers, whose fast attack and slow release already are a pluck.

modes.description: How fast the partial number climbs from string to string. 1 gives modes 1,2,3,4…; 2 gives the odd partials 1,3,5,7…; 0 puts every string on the fundamental, which reads as a rope bridge rather than an instrument.

radius.description: Barrel radius. Larger pushes the near ends of the strings further out past the corners of the frame.

travel.description: How fast the camera slides along the strings. The nodes are fixed in space, so they drift toward the lens as it moves.

ring.description: Vibration rate. Higher modes ring faster than lower ones whatever this is set to, which is the part that matters.

swing.description: Amplitude, as a fraction of the gap to the next string — so a loud band can never swing one string through its neighbour.

gauge.description: String thickness. Bass strings are drawn heavier than treble ones at any setting.

drift.description: How far the barrel axis wanders off the middle of the frame.
